description: Complete 3-week phased MFA rollout plan for Microsoft Entra ID — communication templates, helpdesk FAQ, pilot group strategy, exception handling, and KPI tracking.

phases.name: Preparation
phases.description: Configure registration campaign, identify pilot group, prepare communications, set up break-glass accounts.

tasks.graphAction: Create 2 cloud-only accounts with Global Administrator role, exclude from all CA/registration policies

tasks.task: Enable Authentication Methods Registration Campaign in report-only mode

tasks.graphAction: Create Entra ID security group 'MFA-Pilot-Group', add members per pilot group concept (see pilotGroupConcept)
Send 'Announcement' email template to all users (T-5 days)
Distribute helpdeskFaq section to support staff, walk through top 5 expected ticket types

phases.name: Pilot Rollout
phases.description: Enforce MFA registration for pilot group only. Monitor registration rate and helpdesk ticket volume daily.

tasks.task: Apply registration campaign enforcement to pilot group

tasks.graphAction: Send 'PilotActionRequired' email template to pilot group only
GET /reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails filtered by pilot group — target 90%+ registration by day 4
Short survey or direct follow-up with pilot group on registration experience and clarity of communications

goNoGoCriteria: Helpdesk ticket volume from pilot group manageable (< 1 ticket per 5 users)
No legacy line-of-business application broken by MFA requirement

phases.name: Phased Full Rollout
phases.description: Roll out to remaining users in 2-3 waves. Recommended split: Wave A (next 40%), Wave B (remaining 60% including any flagged exceptions).

tasks.task: Wave A — apply registration campaign to next 40% of users
tasks.graphAction: Update authenticationMethodsRegistrationCampaign includeTargets to add 'MFA-Wave-A' group

tasks.task: Send Wave A 'Action Required' email (T-1 day notice)
tasks.graphAction: Send 'ActionRequired' email template to Wave A group

tasks.task: Monitor Wave A for 3 days, address exceptions
tasks.graphAction: Track registration via reports API, apply exception process (see exceptionProcess) for flagged accounts

tasks.task: Wave B — apply registration campaign to remaining users
tasks.graphAction: Update authenticationMethodsRegistrationCampaign includeTargets = 'All' (minus break-glass and approved exceptions)

tasks.task: Send Wave B 'Action Required' email (T-1 day notice)
tasks.graphAction: Send 'ActionRequired' email template to remaining users
Send 'FinalReminder' email to any users below registration threshold, snoozeDurationInDays = 0

phases.name: Enforcement & Stabilization
phases.description: Switch from registration enforcement to full MFA requirement via Conditional Access. Monitor for one week post-enforcement.

tasks.task: Verify tenant-wide registration rate >= 98% (excluding approved exceptions)
tasks.graphAction: GET /reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails — confirm coverage before enabling CA003

tasks.task: Enable CA003 (Require MFA for All Users) — switch from report-only to On
tasks.graphAction: PATCH /identity/conditionalAccess/policies/{ca003-id} — state = 'enabled'. Cross-reference: CA Hardening Pack policy CA003.
Send completion email to all users with summary and ongoing support info
Daily check of sign-in logs for MFA-related failures, monitor helpdesk ticket trends

pilotGroupConcept.sizeRecommendation: 5-10% of total user count, minimum 5 users, maximum 25 for tenants up to 300 users
selectionCriteria: Include at least 2 IT/helpdesk staff (early feedback, technical fluency)
Include 1-2 executives or department heads (visible champions, smooths broader rollout)
Include a mix of device types (Windows, Mac, mobile-only users)
Include at least 1 user known to be less tech-comfortable (surfaces UX issues for everyone else)
Avoid including anyone on critical deadline work during the pilot week (e.g. finance during month-end close)

groupSetup.graphAction: Create a dedicated Entra ID security group (e.g. 'MFA-Pilot-Group') via /groups endpoint, add selected members via /groups/{id}/members/$ref
groupSetup.rationale: A dedicated group allows the registration campaign and any interim Conditional Access policies to be scoped precisely, and makes rollback trivial if the pilot surfaces blocking issues.

exceptionProcess.principle: Exceptions should be rare, time-boxed, and documented. An exception is never permanent without a documented compensating control.
validReasons: Service accounts that cannot perform interactive MFA (must use Conditional Access app/service principal exclusions, not user exclusions)
Shared/kiosk devices with a single shared account (recommend migrating to dedicated accounts + Temporary Access Pass instead of exclusion)
Temporary technical limitation (e.g. legacy line-of-business app integration pending vendor update) — must have a remediation deadline
invalidReasons: "User doesn't want to install an app on their personal phone" — offer hardware token or phone call/SMS as alternative, do not exempt
"It's inconvenient" — not a valid exception under any circumstance
Executive requesting blanket exemption — escalate to documented risk acceptance signed by leadership, time-boxed to 30 days max
process: 1. Exception request submitted with business justification and proposed expiry date
2. IT Admin reviews against validReasons list
3. If approved: user/account added to a dedicated 'MFA-Exception-Approved' group with documented expiry date in audit log
4. Exception group is excluded only from the specific policy needed (never from all security policies)
5. Exception reviewed at expiry — renewed only with updated justification, or remediated
exceptionProcess.breakGlassNote: Break-glass emergency access accounts (see CA Hardening Pack, Section 6) are NOT the same as MFA exceptions. Break-glass accounts are for emergency admin access only, never used for daily work, and excluded from ALL conditional access and registration policies permanently.

kpis.definition: Percentage of active users with at least one strong authentication method registered
Number of support tickets tagged with MFA/authentication issues
kpis.target: < 1 ticket per 5 users during pilot, < 1 per 10 users during full rollout
kpis.graphSource: External — helpdesk ticketing system, tag-based filter

kpis.definition: Percentage of users with 2+ methods registered (redundancy against lockout)
Percentage of MFA challenges that succeed (vs. timeout/failure)
kpis.graphSource: Entra Sign-in logs filtered by 'Authentication requirement = Multifactor authentication'

kpis.definition: Number of accounts in MFA-Exception-Approved group
Calendar days from rollout start (Phase 0) to CA003 enforcement (Phase 3)
kpis.target: 21 days (3 weeks) per this plan; longer for tenants >300 users
kpis.graphSource: Internal tracking — no Graph API source

ms365dscMapping.note: The registration campaign configuration (authenticationMethodsRegistrationCampaign) maps to AADAuthenticationMethodPolicyAuthenticator. The final enforcement step (enf002) maps directly to the CA003 policy already defined in the CA Hardening Pack's AADConditionalAccessPolicy resource block. Phase 2 export will provide combined .ps1 configuration covering both this kit and the CA Hardening Pack.

crossSell.rationale: This kit prepares the user population for CA003 (Require MFA for All Users), which is delivered as part of the CA Hardening Pack. Customers who purchase this kit alone will reach Phase 3 with a policy reference (enf002) that requires the CA Hardening Pack to execute — cross-sell prompt recommended at Phase 2 completion.
